symptom: A codec-created page stores CanvasWidth/CanvasHeight and PopupWidth/PopupHeight as BSON int32 where every Studio Pro page stores int64; within one page CREATE (codec, int32) and ALTER's page-level SET (page mutator, int64) disagree. mx check is 0 errors either way (ako/mxcli#1264, mendixlabs/mxcli#675). Not only pages: every Integer property the codec writes (flow connection indices, TabIndex, layout-grid weights, ListView PageSize, DecimalPrecision, GlyphIcon Code, mapping MinOccurs/LevelOfParent, workflow thresholds via addInt32) came out int32
cause: modelsdk/gen binds the metamodel's Integer as property.Primitive[int32] (304+ bindings, 331 reached through the registry), and Primitive.BSONValue returned p.Get() unchanged, so the Go width became the stored width. The read side (DecodeInt32) already accepted int32/int64/double, which is why nothing failed on read. The backend's addInt32 helper is a Primitive[int32] too, so the raw-built mapping/workflow/rest elements inherited the same width
file: `modelsdk/property/primitive.go` (BSONValue widens int32 -> int64); reader `mdl/backend/modelsdk/mapping_read.go` (customHandlerFromRaw LevelOfParent); `modelsdk/codec/bsondoc.go` (GetInt32); `mdl/backend/pagemutator/mutator.go` (MaxFileSize default width); tests `modelsdk/codec/intwidth_1264_test.go`, `mdl/backend/modelsdk/int_width_1264_test.go`
insight: **Census before choosing the scope, and the census settles it**: an earlier finding said 'keep a stored int's width (int32 vs int64)', which reads as if Studio Pro stored some Integers as int32 and argued for an exception list. Walking 15,354 Studio Pro-authored units (a pristine `mx create-project` 11.13.0 app plus the .mpr inside eight .mpk packages, Mendix 10.6.4-11.13.0) found 208,038 integer values with typed-array markers excluded, all int64 and 0 int32 (the only other numbers: 154 doubles, all NewSortIndex, which gen binds float64). Every one of the 137 gen Integer properties that occurs is int64-only, so the blanket widening needs no exceptions; the 'keep the width' rule exists only for documents an OLDER mxcli wrote. Corroborated by canon's studiopro_property_defaults.json: when `mx convert` fills an absent Integer it writes $numberLong. **Enumerate the class from the registry, not from a list**: TestEncoder_EveryIntegerPropertyIsInt64 walks codec.DefaultRegistry (new TypeNames()) and sets every Primitive[int32] it finds - 331 properties on 173 types, more than a static grep of gen found (304 on 162), with a >=300 floor against a vacuous pass. **Widening the writer breaks narrow readers of mxcli's OWN output**: customHandlerFromRaw read LevelOfParent with Int32OK only, so it was already wrong for every Studio Pro document (ancestor binding read as source 'parent', level -1) and would have become wrong for mxcli's too; TestCustomHandler_AncestorLevelRoundTrips is the encode->read round trip that catches it. Sweep `.(int32)`, `Int32OK()`, `.Int32()` (panics on int64 - one test did) and `!= int32(` interface comparisons, then ignore the `[0]` marker probes. Five tests pinned int32 on the encoded side; each asserted a width Studio Pro never writes (GlyphIcon Code 570/570 int64, FileManager MaxFileSize 26/26, DecimalPrecision 4,856/4,856). **canon is width-blind** (renderScalar formats with %v), so int32-vs-int64 never counted as a change: no Replaced->Unchanged shift and no new churn, but also no migration - an mxcli-written int32 stays on disk until the element is next genuinely rewritten. mx check accepts both widths, so the e2e evidence is a BSON census of the written project on a fixed and a fault-forced build (pristine 11.13.0 app, the bug-test plus eight doctype scripts): fault-forced 2,970 int32 values on 67 (type, key), fixed 0, mx check 0 errors on BOTH. The sharpest symptom is not on CREATE: under the old build a title-only describe->edit->exec of a Studio Pro page (MyFirstModule.Home_Web) narrowed all 154 of its integers to int32, so every genuine edit of a Studio Pro document carried a whole-document width diff; the fixed build keeps 154/154 int64
